page: Amazon Web Services m7a.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. It features 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in multi-core processing and memory bandwidth. The server achieves top 10% placement in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU scores, and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory read-only bandwidth reaches 25059.68 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 657.74 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic and vector execution are supported by AVX-512 and AES instruction sets, yielding top-tier results in PassMark encryption and extended instruction tests. However, single-threaded operations such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform in the average range.

This bare-metal instance offers high resource density, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for large-scale deployments that require direct hardware access without hypervisor overhead. It is highly capable for multi-threaded workloads, including Redis database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and LLM prompt processing. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff to consider for data-intensive applications.
